chunks: My father narrated to him, may God be pleased with him, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ali ibn al-Salt narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi narrated to me, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The disciples said to Jesus ibn Maryam: 'O Teacher of the good, teach us which of the things is the hardest?' He said: 'The hardest of things is the wrath of God, the Exalted, the Sublime.' They asked: 'By what is the wrath of God avoided?' He said: 'By not getting angry.' They asked: 'What is the beginning of anger?' He said: 'Haughtiness, oppressiveness, and belittling of people.'

key_terms.الْحَوَارِيُّونَ: The disciples of Jesus (peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What is the root cause of anger and how can one avoid God's wrath according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, the disciples of Jesus (peace be upon him) inquire about the most formidable spiritual obstacle, which is identified as the wrath of God. The Imam clarifies that divine wrath is averted by mastering one's own anger, which itself stems from the root vices of arrogance (kibr), self-importance (tajabbur), and belittling others. This chain of causality highlights the Shia emphasis on internal character refinement as the key to divine favor.
